question: What percentage of tests will be positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 1 (New England) for the week ending September 26, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in HHS Region 1 (New England) for the week ending 2026-09-26 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
# RSV test positivity in HHS Region 1 (New England), week ending 2026-09-26

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on CDC NREVSS dataset rgnm-fkqb (field `percent_pos`, `level='Region 1'`, `pathogen='RSV'`), as posted on 2026-10-30. I queried it through the Socrata API. [data.cdc.gov API](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- 2026-08-29 (latest week I'm reporting): RSV was 0.40% positive, 7 detections out of 1,748 tests. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Two caveats about my data pull:
  - I ran the query today, so the values reflect any revisions made since early September.
  - I left out rows for weeks published after 2026-09-07.
- Precision is limited: with about 1,500 to 1,750 tests a week, each extra positive test moves the rate by about 0.06 percentage points. Some weeks hide their counts (shown as "*").

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The target week had not happened as of 2026-09-07.
- RSV in New England is at summer lows, under 1%, though somewhat above the levels of past summers.
- 2026-09-03: a British Columbia report said US RSV activity was "very low in most areas of the country." [BCCDC](https://www.bccdc.ca/Health-Info-Site/Documents/Respiratory_data/respiratory_surveillance_2026-09-03.pdf)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-03: BCCDC said US RSV activity was very low in most areas. [BCCDC](https://www.bccdc.ca/Health-Info-Site/Documents/Respiratory_data/respiratory_surveillance_2026-09-03.pdf)
- 2026-03 to 2026-04: the 2025-26 season peaked late and ran long.
  - Region 1 peaked at 10.29% (week ending 2026-01-31) and 10.20% (week ending 2026-02-14).
  - Positivity stayed above 1% until the week ending 2026-06-06.
  - Maine extended its RSV season through April 2026. [Maine CDC advisory](https://www.maine.gov/dhhs/mecdc/sites/maine.gov.dhhs.mecdc/files/health-professionals/advisories/2026-03-Create%20Health%20Advisories/2026PHADV005RSVCirculation.pdf), [Pharmacy Times](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/late-season-rsv-surge-extends-risk-into-spring-challenging-seasonal-expectations-expert-says)
- An undated Becker's piece said CDC modeling showed RSV "likely growing in Maine." I could not confirm when it was published. [Becker's](https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/quality/public-health/rsv-lingers-in-parts-of-us-even-as-flu-and-covid-19-recede/)

## 4. Base rates (Region 1 RSV % positive, current dataset)

**2026 summer, weekly:**
- July: 0.45, 0.45, 0.80, 0.44
- August: 0.31, 0.92, 0.63, 0.23, 0.40
- Mean is about 0.5, range 0.23 to 0.92.

**Same weeks in earlier years (late August, then September):**

| Season | Late Aug | Sep wk 1 | Sep wk 2 | Sep wk 3 | Last Sep week | Early Oct |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 0.46 (08-30) | 0.23 (09-06) | 0.31 (09-13) | 0.43 (09-20) | **0.39 (09-27)** | 0.44 (10-04) |
| 2024 | 0.25 (08-31) | 0.21 (09-07) | 0.03 (09-14) | 0.27 (09-21) | **0.48 (09-28)** | 0.73 (10-05) |
| 2023 | 1.01 (08-26) | 0.99 (09-02) | 1.48 (09-09) | 0.68 (09-16), 1.72 (09-23) | **2.59 (09-30)** | 2.47 (10-07) |

- 2023 was an early, large season, and it is the only recent year where late-September positivity came close to the 2.5 ceiling of the question's range.
- Change over four weeks, from late August to the last week of September:
  - 2025: -0.07 points
  - 2024: +0.23 points
  - 2023: +1.58 points
- In the last week of September, positivity is usually flat or starting a slow rise.
- Week-to-week noise is roughly ±0.2 to 0.4 points at these levels. For example, 2024 went 0.21, 0.03, 0.27 in consecutive weeks.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets on this series.
- I found no expert forecast specific to Region 1.
- CDC publishes national RSV growth estimates (Rt), but I did not find a Region 1 value from before 2026-09-07.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly NREVSS updates will add the weeks ending 09-05 through 09-26. Earlier weeks can be revised, and the 2026-10-30 posting is the one that counts.
- New England schools reopen in late August and early September, which typically drives the start of RSV's autumn rise. Regional RSV onset usually comes in October or later.
- Fall immunization campaigns start around this time: nirsevimab/clesrovimab for infants, maternal vaccine, and older-adult vaccines. They are unlikely to change late-September positivity much.
- 2026-09-10: the American Lung Association published a release saying respiratory virus season starts in October. This is after the cutoff date and is context only. [press release](https://digital-release.wowktv.com/business/press-releases/cision/20260910DC44273/how-new-englanders-can-protect-their-health-during-respiratory-virus-season)
